reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern is a highly regular, piecewise-linear sawtooth waveform with a fundamental period of 55 points, as confirmed by the dataset metadata and consistent cycle counts across candidates. Each cycle consists of a rapid linear ascent (≈10–12 points) from a trough near -1.0 to a peak near +1.7–2.2, followed by a slower, multi-step descent (≈40–43 points) via plateaus and gentle drops back to the trough. Baseline level varies modestly across segments (median ranging from -0.22 to +0.44), but the shape—especially the steep rise and stepped decay—is invariant. Amplitude (90th percentile range) is consistently ~2.5–3.0 robust-standardized units. Peaks are sharp and symmetrically truncated; troughs are flat-bottomed and stable near -1.0. Noise is negligible: roughness is zero in all catalog entries, and visual inspection shows no high-frequency jitter—transitions are clean stepwise changes. Minor variations exist in slope per point (±0.014) and curvature (near-zero), but these reflect baseline shifts rather than morphological deviation. Acceptable variation includes ±0.3 in median level, ±0.2 in peak height, and slight differences in plateau durations during descent; however, the core 55-point cadence and asymmetric rise/fall asymmetry must be preserved.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer reference 0 for queries with single-cycle or ambiguous length; it is the cleanest exemplar. Use reference 1 for queries matching 3-cycle structure with moderate baseline shift. Reference 2 is suitable when query shows elevated baseline but intact morphology; reference 3 should only be used when query exhibits 5+ cycles and higher amplitude—explicitly discount its double-trough artifact region. Always align by local cycle phase (rise onset), not absolute x-index.
